title: Real-valued form of a Boolean function
statement: For a function $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, its real-valued form is the function on the same domain obtained by encoding each Boolean output as a real number.
caveat: The snippet does not include the definition of the Boolean-to-real encoding, so its specific values cannot be stated from the supplied ground truth.
